question.problem:
Which of the following sets are infinite?

I. $A={{f}^{(n)}(x)=\frac{{\text{d}}^{n}}{\text{d}{x}^{n}}({e}^{1-2x})\,:\,n\in {N}_{0}}$

II. $B={{g}^{(n)}(x)=\frac{{\text{d}}^{n}}{\text{d}{x}^{n}}(3{e}^{x})\,:\,n\in {N}_{0}}$

III. $C={{h}^{(n)}(x)=\frac{{\text{d}}^{n}}{\text{d}{x}^{n}}(4{e}^{-x})\,:\,n\in {N}_{0}}$
question.worked_solution:
The cardinality of a finite set is the number of elements contained within it. A set is infinite if it has infinitely many elements.

- The set $A$ is infinite. Listing the first few elements of our set, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{(0)}(x) & ={e}^{1-2x} \\ {f}^{(1)}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({e}^{1-2x})=-2{e}^{1-2x} \\ {f}^{(2)}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-2{e}^{1-2x})=4{e}^{1-2x} \\ {f}^{(3)}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(4{e}^{1-2x})=-8{e}^{1-2x} \\ ⋮\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, we can write our set as follows:

$$
A={{e}^{1-2x},-2{e}^{1-2x},4{e}^{1-2x},-8{e}^{1-2x},…}
$$

Consequently, $A$ is infinite.

- The set $B$ is finite. Listing the first few elements of our set, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}^{(0)}(x) & =3{e}^{x} \\ {g}^{(1)}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3{e}^{x})=3{e}^{x} \\ {g}^{(2)}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3{e}^{x})=3{e}^{x} \\ {g}^{(3)}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3{e}^{x})=3{e}^{x} \\ ⋮\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, $B$ contains only one element:

$$
B={3{e}^{x}}
$$

Consequently, $|B|=1,$ which is finite.

- The set $C$ is finite. Listing the first few elements of our set, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{h}^{(0)}(x) & =4{e}^{-x} \\ {h}^{(1)}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(4{e}^{-x})=-4{e}^{-x} \\ {h}^{(2)}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-4{e}^{-x})=4{e}^{-x} \\ {h}^{(3)}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(4{e}^{-x})=-4{e}^{-x} \\ ⋮\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, $C$ contains only two elements:

$$
C={4{e}^{-x},-4{e}^{-x}}.
$$

Consequently, $|C|=2,$ which is finite.

Therefore, the correct answer is "$A$ only."
